title: Surjective π0 maps induce closed immersions of underlying ∞-topoi
statement_scope: Whole Proposition 1.2.7: let φ: A → B be a map of connective E∞-rings which induces a surjection π0A → π0B. Then the corresponding map f: Spec B → Spec A induces a closed immersion of underlying ∞-topoi.

standard_prerequisites: §V.2.2 identification of the underlying topos of Spec A with Shv((CAlg_A^et)^op).
Proposition VII.8.10 on the structure of étale morphisms.
Theorem VII.4.1 on enough points for hypercompletions.
Corollary 1.1.7 and Proposition 1.1.4 (author PDF pp. 6-7) on points and strictly Henselian quotients.
difficulty_reason: Rule author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: H2 because the proof at author PDF pp. 12-13 identifies the relevant ∞-topoi as sheaves on étale algebras, shows f* is conservative by factoring each étale B-algebra through an explicit pushout using Proposition VII.8.10, then proves the unit of f* f_* is an equivalence by checking on points via Corollary 1.1.7 and Proposition 1.1.4. This is a concrete non-routine ∞-topos argument, but a supporting closed-immersion criterion rather than the H3 main comparison.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Explicit étale-algebra pushout factorization, conservativity of f*, and pointwise hypercompleteness to identify the closed subtopos.
